newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen higher at opening.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen higher at opening.

text.p: Wall Street stocks will head higher at the opening if the third quarter preliminary gross domestic product comes in on target and sparks another rally in the bond market, analysts said.
But analysts said bonds may not have much farther to go and a rally without the high techs would be shaky.

"The GDP is expected to come in lower, so I guess bonds will rally, but I don't know how much higher they can go after Tuesday's move before we get some profit taking," said Hildergard Zagorski, analyst at Prudential Securities.

Preliminary third quarter GDP is expected to rise 1.8 percent against a previous 4.7 percent increase. Other economic news today includes September new home sales and the Federal Reserve's Beige Book of economic conditions. Both are due at 1000 EST/1500 GMT.
The Treasury's 30-year bond soared nearly two points on Tuesday and its yield sank to 6.68 percent -- its lowest level since April 4 and compared with 6.84 percent on Monday.
Zagorski said that in order for the stock market to show strength today, high techs would have to take part in any upward move. The sector was battered yesterday.
"The techs have been weak and unless they stabilize, I don't see the market doing much of anything," she said.

"You can't run on the blue chips alone. Yesterday, the rest of market was just marking time and most of the interest was in the Dow Industrial Average. I don't think we're going to rush ahead to new highs from here. We are in a mildly corrective phase which leads to a choppy market."
In Tokyo, the Nikkei Average fell 276 points to 20,682.
In London, the FTSE 100 Index was down 16 at 3978.

Among U.S. shares traded in London, Philip Morris Cos Inc was up 1/4 at 94, Chrysler Corp was up 1/4 at 33-7/8, Compaq Computer Corp was up 3/8 at 67-7/8, Digital Equipment Corp was up 1/4 at 29-3/4 and Hewlett-Packard Co was up 3/8 to 44-5/8.
U.S. treasuries were steady, with the long bond up 2/32 to yield 6.68 percent.
The dollar was just above 114 yen in Tokyo and firmer in Europe.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street writes that Washington Post Co has been buying cable systems in out-of-the-way places based on the idea that, without the heavy competition of large urban areas, these smaller systems will not require as much expensive new technology or face the same profit pressure.
The New York Times writes that the stock of Donna Karan International Inc took a beating, falling 17 percent on the New York Stock Exchange after releasing poor quarterly earnings.
